we have successfully expressed Δ15- and Δ4-desaturates in a mammalian cell line and that the combination of these two desaturases results in a fatty acid composition that has a more desirable n-6/n3 ratio and a higher DHA level.
we have successfully expressed two non-mammal Δ4-desaturates in HEK293 cells.

we successfully heterologously expressed two non-mammal Δ4-desaturates in HEK293 cells, which could directly convert DPA to DHA, and the cooperation of the two desaturases could produce a more desirable fatty acids composition in mammalian cells.

the development of new strategies for improving fatty acid compositions in mammalian cells and animals.
the development of a more desirable fatty acids composition, and it has been achieved by the heterologous expression in mammalian cells of the two genes coding for Δ15/ Δ4-desaturates.
the biosynthesis of DPA from ARA, and the subsequent conversion of DPA to DHA by Δ4-desaturates, and the conversion of ARA to EPA and DHA by Δ15-desaturates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the heterologous expression in mammalian cells of Δ15/ Δ4-desaturates from E. gracilis and S. canaliculatus respectively, can achieve a desirable fatty acid composition in the cell membrane phospholipids.

the expression of non-mammalian Δ15 and Δ4 desaturases in mammalian cells is a feasible way to produce a more desirable fatty acids composition, which may be applied in transgenic animals for producing such a fatty acids profile in their products.

the Δ4-desaturation step is a very efficient pathway for the conversion of DPA into DPA, and the cooperation of the Δ15-desaturases with Δ4-desaturates can make a desirable fatty acid composition with high levels of DHA, EPA and ARA in transgenic mammalian cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Δ15/Δ6-desaturase pathway in transgenic animals is more feasible than the Δ5/Δ6-desaturation pathway, which is the only way for producing n-3 PFA in mammals.
the Δ15/Δ6-desaturases and the Δ4-desatuarase are all very useful for improving the fatty acid composition in mammals.

we have successfully expressed the two non-mammal genes, E. gracilisΔ4-desaturase gene (EgΔ4-desatur) and S. canaliculatusΔ4-desaturate gene (SccΔ4-desatur), in the mammalian cells.
